comments.author: @wafiv
comments.text: Economist here: The downfall of AirBnB is when people thought they could run a business model that looked like a hotel versus a small mom and pop business that required them to be hands on. Hotels are able to hire maids who clean an entire floor of rooms (20-30) per day. Their per room cost once broken down is extremely cheap. That is not true for an AirBnB where you are paying a cleaning company likely and having to clean it everyday is honestly not economical. You have 2-3 rooms at most, with hotels having hundreds. The truth is, if you want to run an AirBnb and make money, you either have to do the cleaning yourself or you need to require minimum stays of 4 days.

comments.text: My  husband and I have been using VRBO for years for vacation b/c we like to get a house with a kitchen for cooking, a garage for parking, and a private hot tub, but we look at the reviews to make sure the house and host are good.  Some prices are crazy for hot tubs, but we have found some good prices in very pretty locations in NM and CO.  We also take our two cats with us so we need a house that allows cats and a bedroom for them.  Cleaning fees are generally more reasonable but check out rules generally include taking out the trash, putting dishes in the dishwasher and towels in the washer and starting them before leaving, not too bad in my opinion.  But at our last house there was one thing I laughed at, even though it allowed cats and dogs in the house there was a sign that said "pets are not allowed on furniture"  I laughed b/c you can't allow cats and expect them to not jump on furniture.  And it listed an extra cleaning fee if there was excessive pet hair left, so we quickly vacuumed the couches where our white cat had left some fur.  Still prefer VRBO, for now.

Almost every place that had a pool charged a daily fee of like $20-30 per person per day to use.  I put in a reservation for one that seemed pretty reasonable until they told me they had cameras inside the rental and they would be recording everything I do.  I cancelled that reservation faster than a bullet.  

I stick with hotels now.  They can be pricy and not terribly private but at least I don't have to clean and aren't charged absurd fees.
